<p>
I am a Ph.D. Candidate at Northwestern University in the Department of
Political Science. My research examines heterogeneity within group politics,
with a particular focus on how migration and identity shape political
attitudes and behavior. My dissertation project, <em>Borders Beyond Borders:
Migration, Identity, and the Transnational Political Behavior of the Eritrean
Diaspora</em>, investigates the political and identity socialization processes
that Black immigrants undergo in their home countries and in the United
States. I conduct an in-depth case study of Eritrean immigrants in the United
States to illustrate the profound impact salient events in the home country,
migration pathways, and transnational politics have on shaping the process of
identity formation and political behavior. Ultimately, my project illuminates
novel theoretical and empirical insights that help bridge literatures in Race
and Ethnicity, American, and Comparative Politics by emphasizing the importance
of geopolitical relationships in the formation of identity and political
behavior. My work has been supported through the National Science Foundation
Graduate Research Fellowship, the American Political Science Association, and
the Northwestern University Graduate School.
</p>

## Research

My research focuses on heterogeneity within group politics, with broader interests in
race and ethnicity, migration, and political behavior. 


My current research projects investigate:

- **Borders Beyond Borders: Migration, Identity, and the Transnational Political Behavior of 
the Eritrean Diaspora** — How the process of identity formation and political socialization is shaped through transnational processes.
- **Black and Ethnic: Theorizing New Approaches to the Study of Black Immigrants in
the United States** — Investigates how aggregation bias in the study of Black immigrants can obscure meaningful within group heterogeneity.
- **Investigating the Naturalization Gap: Determinants of
Immigrant Political Participation in the US** — Explores how time to naturalization in the US has impacts on immigrant political participation.
